description: Advanced ECG concepts including axis determination, bundle branch blocks, and complex arrhythmias
overview: This module covers advanced ECG interpretation techniques including electrical axis determination, bundle branch blocks, and complex arrhythmia analysis.
objectives: Determine electrical axis using various methods
Apply systematic approach to difficult cases

slides.title: Electrical Axis Determination
slides.content: Electrical axis represents the overall direction of ventricular depolarization. Normal axis: -30° to +90°. Methods include quadrant method, isoelectric lead method, and hexaxial reference system.

slides.title: Bundle Branch Blocks
slides.content: Right bundle branch block: QRS >0.12s, RSR' in V1, wide S in V6. Left bundle branch block: QRS >0.12s, wide R in V6, no Q waves in I, V5-V6.

quiz.question: What is the characteristic pattern of right bundle branch block?
quiz.explanation: Right bundle branch block is characterized by RSR' pattern in V1.

slides.title: Complex Arrhythmias
slides.content: Complex arrhythmias include multifocal atrial tachycardia, junctional rhythms, escape rhythms, and pacemaker rhythms. Each requires careful analysis of P waves, QRS morphology, and rhythm patterns.

quiz.question: What characterizes multifocal atrial tachycardia?
options: Three or more P wave morphologies
quiz.explanation: Multifocal atrial tachycardia is characterized by three or more different P wave morphologies.

slides.title: Systematic Approach to Difficult Cases
slides.content: Systematic approach: 1) Rate and rhythm, 2) Axis, 3) Intervals, 4) Morphology, 5) Clinical correlation. Always consider the clinical context and patient presentation.

quiz.question: What is the final step in systematic ECG interpretation?
quiz.explanation: Clinical correlation is the final and most important step in ECG interpretation.
